correctness.rationale: Arc endpoint integrations and Newton identities establish the exact minimal-arc rigidity. Unit-circle self-inversive coefficients force roots of two regular polygons. The real-linear Jacobian is derived with the explicit normalization and area/rotation gauge; conjugate-frequency pairs and even-order Nyquist sector give the two squared singular values with k-1 real multiplicities each. All are strictly positive for 0<rho<1. The inverse function theorem then gives the sharp local bound. A standalone executable passed 144 numerical singular-spectrum and finite-difference checks; the universal conclusion relies on the displayed proof.

value.rationale: Perfect energy balancing of a consecutive Fourier band is a natural sampling-mask design problem. The theorem determines minimal geometric complexity and equality rigidity, then supplies an exact noise sensitivity certificate for recovering 2k-2 endpoint degrees of freedom from exactly 2k-2 real Fourier data. The universal occupancy-only condition number and unique half-occupancy isotropic regime are structural, not a numerical tweak or a routine reparameterization.
